newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable despite weaker crudes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable despite weaker crudes.

text.p: Naphtha prices hardly budged in afternoon Tokyo trade on Tuesday despite moderate losses in overnight crude oil prices, buttressed by tight physical supplies for prompt cargoes, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half April was quoted at $233.00/235.00, little changed from late Monday levels. First-half May was bid at $230.00, against offers at $232.00.
In spreads, second-half April/second-half May was assessed at plus $6.00/7.00.
On Monday, first-half April/first-half May was traded at plus $9.00, indicating firm sentiment for near-term cargoes.
Also on Monday, first-half May/first-half June was sold to a Japanese trading house at plus $5.50.
A major oil firm said it bought about 25,000 tonnes of jet kerosene cargo for mid-March delivery. The price was at around $2.00 over the mean of Singapore quotes.
Idemitsu Petrochemical joined Mitsubishi Chemical and Showa Denko in cutting ethylene output to help raise wholesale prices for its petrochemical products.
The company said it had cut ethylene production by 12 percent at its 365,000-tonne-per-year Chiba plant.
